served: video-EEG monitoring of a typical event
results: 1. interictal EEG: runs of generalized polyspikes and spike-wave discharges at 2-3 Hz lasting 3-4 s, predominating bifrontally and occasionally shifting laterally

2. video-EEG monitoring of a typical event: ictal body turning preceded by head version; although the clinical onset looked focal, the EEG showed generalized beta fast activity for 0.5 s followed by a generalized 2.5-3 Hz spike-wave discharge with maximum bifrontal amplitude
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Genetic generalized epilepsy, with generalized-onset tonic–clonic seizures showing focal-appearing head version and body turning (generalized epilepsy with focal semiology)

ALTERNATIVES:  
1. Focal epilepsy with very rapid secondary bilateral synchrony  
2. Symptomatic generalized epilepsy, such as Lennox–Gastaut syndrome  
3. Psychogenic nonepileptic events occurring in a patient with incidental generalized epileptiform discharges
